content.question: What is the total number of modules covered in the 360 degree complete Android development series?
content.explanation: The course consists of a total of 11 modules starting from Android introduction and ending with publishing the app on Google Play Store. Each module builds upon the previous one to create a comprehensive learning path.
hints: Look for the phrase 'total of' in the introduction
The number is mentioned at the beginning of the course roadmap
It comes before the discussion of individual modules

content.question: In which module will you learn about Jetpack Compose?
content.explanation: Jetpack Compose, the modern toolkit for building native Android apps, is introduced in the fourth module. After learning UI components in module 2 and Kotlin in module 3, you'll be ready to use Jetpack Compose.
hints: It comes after Kotlin is introduced
It's described as the modern toolkit
Count the modules in the roadmap

content.question: What is the topic of the seventh module in the Android development series?
content.explanation: The seventh module focuses on application architecture, where you will explore the MVVM pattern, use ViewModel, and work with LiveData. These are essential architectural components for building scalable Android applications.
hints: It comes after the networking module
It discusses MVVM pattern
It involves ViewModel and LiveData

content.question: Which module covers internal and external storage methods?
content.explanation: The fifth module focuses on data storage and covers both internal and external storage methods, as well as how to use remote databases to manage structured data within your app.
hints: Data storage comes after basic UI and language learning
It's before networking discussions
It deals with information persistence

content.question: In the building analogy used in the course, what does the user interface of an app compare to?

options.text: The vibrant colours and windows of the building

content.explanation: The building analogy compares the app's user interface (buttons, illustrations, layouts) to the building's vibrant colours, windows, doors, and shapes. This represents the visible and interactive parts of the application.
hints: Think about what users see in an app
The building has colours and windows
It's about visual elements

content.question: What does data pipelines in an Android app compare to in a building?
content.explanation: Data pipelines in an Android app are compared to the electricity and water pipelines in a building. Both deliver essential resources (data/utilities) to different parts of the system, allowing seamless flow and operation.
hints: Think about how data flows through an app
Buildings have pipelines for utilities
It's about delivery systems

content.question: Which module in the Android series focuses on building a complete Android application using all learned concepts?
content.explanation: The ninth module is where everything comes together. You will build a complete Android application using all the concepts, tools, and techniques learned in the previous modules.
hints: It's described as 'where it all comes together'
It comes after Firebase integration
It's before the testing module

content.question: What is the final step covered in the eleventh module of the Android development series?

options.text: Publishing your app on Google Play Store

content.explanation: The eleventh and final module teaches how to publish your app on the Google Play Store. This is the last step in the complete Android development journey, allowing you to release your app to users worldwide.
hints: It's the last module number
Think about what comes after development is complete
It involves releasing to users

content.question: What does an Android application consist of, according to the course definition?

options.text: Various components like UI, controllers, APIs, backend, databases, and AI/ML modules

content.explanation: An Android application is made up of various interconnected components including the user interface, controllers, APIs, backend servers, databases, and even AI/ML modules. When connected in an organized way, these create a fully functional, scalable application.
hints: Think of all the parts that make an app work
The building analogy mentions multiple components
It's not just one thing but many working together

content.question: How many smartphones globally are powered by Android according to the introduction?
content.explanation: Android is the most widely used mobile operating system globally and powers over 3.3 billion smartphones. This makes it one of the most important platforms to learn for mobile app development.
hints: It's mentioned at the very beginning
Android is used by billions of people
It's more than 3 billion
